thread.subject: Board game organisation and why it should be with origamis only

article.subject: Board game organisation and why it should be with origamis only
article.body:
EDIT : Here's the playlist of the tutorials I've been slowly making.

Thought I'd share how I've been reorganising my board games if that can make people want to do the same for their own games. I am a member of a fantastic group, on Facebook, called Les Ludistes Origamistes. They have their own website that can actually calculate the size of the paper you need for whatever box, divider or card holder you want. Unfortunately everything is in French but nothing you can't figure out. The videos are very straightforward even if you don't speak the language, you just follow what the guy does. I suppose the only words you'll need to know are like largeur (width), longueur (length), épaisseur (thickness), boîte (box), feuille (sheet), taille (size), séparateur/diviseur (divider), cartes (cards) and you should be able to use the website rather easily. Their tutorials are videos you can find on 2 different channels here (Les Ludistes Origamistes) and there (Mémo-règles), but all corresponding videos are on the website too.
I'm actually tempted to make my own videos but strictly in English to share this great knowledge, while obviously still crediting them. I am now origami converted. It makes your boxes beautiful, it eases setup and pack up, and it is really cheap as you'll just need paper/cardstock, scissors, pencils, and a ruler. Also, it looks intimidating at first but once you're in it, you just can't stop. It's addictive.


My very first origamisation was for the board game Nidavellir. I made a box around the coin rack so the coins are always in place and it eases setup by a mile. Also there's boxes with dividers and small corolla boxes as drawers to keep the coins of every player separated. When people are playing, you just take the drawer and give it to them. Great and simple box to make to hold resources (it opens up when you play).


Then I did a full revamp of the Abyss box to welcome all the expansions in the box, as my second organisation. It was a lot of work for the beginner that I was. I actually made a quick video about it as I streamed the whole process on Twitch. It eases setup as well as you just take the boxes out of the cardboard box, open them, and place them on the table. Then when it is done, you just put everything back in the box and it's done!

Legendary Inventors and its original not paper hungry boxes to hold the players' cubes. Also like for a few other board game boxes, I made my own insert with dividers cause the cardboard divider was actually useless.

Probably my biggest pride is the card shoes made for the decks of It's A Wonderful World and Dune : Imperium. These are the combination of a Moda Masu box with 2 Baggi boxes. When in the box, it holds the cards still. When you want to play, you pull the top Baggi box and push the side strips of the Moda Masu. Then you lock the edges with the Baggi box. It makes a tray where it is easy and quick to draw cards while staying still on the table.

One of my most recent works as I received Stardew Valley fairly recently. I also streamed the process and made a video about it. It was a lot of work but totally worth it as the box can actually close now. It used to be impossible because with the two trays and the fish + minerals/artifacts bags, the box would be too full to close properly. Now everything is easy to pull out of the box when you desire to play and it closes properly too.

I obviously won't post all the origamisations I've made but I made a small album on Imgur if that interests anyone. It features other games such as Descent 2nd Edition, Detective Club, Dune : Imperium, Game of Thrones 1st Edition, Human Punishment Social Deduction 2.0, Not Alone, Sagrada with 5-6p expansion, Sushi Go! Party, When I Dream...
My next projects will probably be Dream Runners, Wingspan and Red Rising. Also a quick origamisation of BANG! would be great too (too many cards that go everywhere in the box).


The other not so obvious advantage to convert yourself to origamising your games is that it keeps your cat busy instead of knocking everything off the table. The cat will think you just took a bed out for him and will be delighted! 😁

article.subject: Re: Board game organisation and why it should be with origamis only
article.body:
Thank you so much. I actually had a quick look, I am not sure how to post on it with the links to the board games. I am rather new to the forums of BGG.

The basic Masu boxes (the ones that are mainly used in this list) are really easy to make and I definitely started there too! But I prefer to be able to have boxes of specific measurements instead of all boxes to be squares and with a height of half the length of the box so that is why I was tempted to try to share this knowledge with others. 😄 Seems like this community is pretty big among the French board gamers on Facebook, but living in Australia, all my friends are always amazed at my boxes. Seems pretty unknown here and people just buy expensive inserts instead.

For the V pockets, I believe they're actually the first thing I tried with my Nidavellir cards and was like "Wow, it's that easy!" and then, you couldn't stop me. Very handy and pretty looking holders, imo. When you want to take the card, you open the right strip, and when done, you place your cards in and lock it with the right strip under the left one.
The measurement of the strip of paper you need is fairly simple. Here's the video from their channel. You need the width of a card (example in the video 67mm), and the thickness of the deck (12mm) + 1mm. The strip will be as is :
height : width of the card / example in the video = 67mm
length : (4 x width) + (2 x (thickness of the deck + 1mm)) / example in the video = (4 x 67) + (2 x 13)
Then you just follow what he's doing.

2. Select "Board game"


3. Enter the board game for the origami organization you've done (I've chosen Nidavellir as an example), then you can copy the information in this post you added about Nidavellir! Then at the bottom you will see a "Save" button!

This is inspiring ... all the other organization solutions are pricey (as much as the game or more!) or they require too much crafting skill. I've made cardstock boxes before for card decks, so if it's the same all-thumbs skill level required here, I'm interested!

If "patterns" provided for a given title, even better! Now my stuff will stop falling down when I store vertically.


Honestly, I don't believe it is too difficult to do. Even the more advanced stuff like the card shoe, are a mix of 2 techniques of boxes that you should learn when you start out. Most people start with the basic Masu which is a square box, and the Baggi box which is a rectangular box with a square side, but then you learn about the Moda Masu which is a box to your dimensions and you want to use for literally everything. Not much more complex than the other two, only thing is it takes a tiny bit more time because you have to do your measurements on all sides but once you're used to it, it is quite quick. I rewatched quickly one of my streams and I seemed to take about 10 minutes to make a Moda Masu. So I definitely think reorganising their boxes is for everyone, even the least crafty of us.
And Abyss is great! One of my first modern era board games and that's when I fell in love with Bruno Cathala's games! I love the two expansions as well. To me Abyss is an 8 but with both expansions, it is easily a 10/10. They add great stuff without adding much complexity.
